findings.source_quote: καὶ εἰ κρείττων ἔσται ἢ οὐδὲ ἔσται
findings.english_quote: and whether it will be better or will no longer exist.
findings.issue: “No longer” substitutes a temporal contrast for the emphatic negation οὐδὲ: the alternative is that the world will not even exist. Although cessation is contextually understandable, the draft loses the explicit contrast between being better and not existing at all.
findings.suggested_revision: Render: “and whether it will be better or will not even exist.”

findings.source_quote: καὶ ἵνα μὴ τὸ κατ᾿ εἶδος λέγω, ταῦτά τε καὶ τὰ τούτοις ἑπόμενα μαθεῖν εἶπον θέλειν.
findings.english_quote: And, not to speak item by item, I said that I wanted to learn these things and those that follow from them.”
findings.issue: The closing quotation mark places the retrospective report εἶπον θέλειν inside Clement’s earlier direct speech. The Greek resumes narration by reporting what he said he wanted; the draft instead presents that retrospective report as an additional utterance to his interlocutor.
findings.suggested_revision: Close the direct quotation after the world’s possible nonexistence. Continue outside it: “And, to avoid speaking item by item, I said that I wanted to learn these things and those that follow from them.”

findings.source_quote: ὡς οἶσθα καὶ σύ, μικρῷ τάχιον εἰπὼν ὡς πᾶσα ὑπόθεσις ἀνασκευάζεται καὶ κατασκευάζεται
findings.english_quote: as you yourself know from what I said a little earlier: every thesis can be refuted and established
findings.issue: The explicit local subject σύ supplies the natural referent of εἰπών: the addressee said this earlier. The draft instead supplies the present speaker as the earlier speaker and introduces “from what I said.” Its note acknowledges the second-person reading but gives no grammatical or contextual reason for departing from the explicit local subject; merely stating that εἰπών is taken as first person does not substantiate that attribution.
findings.suggested_revision: Use the source-transparent attachment: “as you yourself know, having said a little earlier that every thesis can be refuted and established.” Any retained first-person proposal would need a substantive source-based explanation, not merely an assertion of the chosen referent.

findings.source_quote: ἀποδείξει γὰρ μιᾷ τῇ ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς καὶ ἀκριβεῖ ἐξετάσει τῇ πανταχόθεν τὰ ὅλα ὀρθῷ εἴληπται λογισμῷ.
findings.english_quote: for through one proof—the exact examination made at the outset and from every side—the whole has been rightly grasped by sound reasoning.
findings.issue: The ordinary construction coordinates a single proof from the outset with a precise examination from every side. The draft instead identifies the examination with the proof and moves “at the outset” into the description of the examination. An explanatory reading of καί can be considered, but the note neither preserves the materially different coordinated reading nor explains why identification is preferred. The current disclosure is therefore insufficient under the supplied ambiguity policy.
findings.suggested_revision: A source-transparent revision is: “for by a single proof from the outset and by a precise examination from every side, everything has been grasped with sound reasoning.” If an explanatory rendering of καί is proposed instead, preserve the coordinated alternative in a note and explain the contextual basis for that choice.
